title: Port regressions
text:
These project-owned cases cover supported behavior, invalid or unsupported inputs, and known differences discovered during development. They are separate from the 2,303 source cases in STACK compliance.
Expected is the behavior recorded for each case. Port is the SymPy implementation, STACK is Maxima, and Browser runs the port through Pyodide. A browser agreement can confirm the same known defect; it does not make that result correct.

Scope and technical details

An expected input-handling check verifies that invalid or unsupported input is correctly refused. It is not a successful mathematical comparison. Known port issues remain defects even when their observations match a recorded exception. Root-convention differences have their own explanation and are not labeled mathematical failures.
The saved run observes isolated Python, official STACK functions where applicable, and the same port in browser Pyodide. “Test applies” is the answer test’s applicability, separate from input syntax validity. Missing observations remain unavailable.

title: STACK compliance
text:
Each source case compares a submitted answer with a reference using a named STACK answer test. The SymPy port implements a subset of STACK; this page shows its coverage gaps, expected behavior, and agreement with STACK and the browser.
Port is this SymPy implementation. STACK is the reference Maxima implementation. Expected is the source fixture’s intended accept, reject, or error result. Only STACK tests with a fully supported equivalent in the Python port were run.

Scope and technical details

This compares CAS answer-test functions rather than complete Moodle grading sessions. The port currently provides eight answer-test families. Cases outside port coverage stay in the inventory and are labeled by the missing answer test or unsupported input/feature. Some direct reference calls are also omitted because they need parser or controller preparation.
“Test applicability” asks whether an answer test can compare the supplied values. It is separate from input syntax validity and from the final accept/reject mark. Form tests such as EqualComAss can reject mathematically equivalent expressions.
Source codes 0 and 1 mean expected rejection and acceptance; -1 expects a controlled error. Codes -2 and -3 flag source-authored native deviations. Only specifically reviewed cases are labeled “Known STACK issue.” Ordinary feedback notes are retained but not generally compared; asserted controlled-error notes are checked separately.
Browser agreement includes input/scope classifications as well as graded results. The summary separates these. STACK coverage counts available observations, not compatibility passes.
